# Regression QA - RC 2.14: transaction-categorization findings

**Test round:** RC 2.14 pre-release categorization pass
**Prepared by:** QA (enrichment)
**Verdict:** Not signed off - the findings below must clear before this build ships

## Summary

The RC 2.14 pass replays our labelled statement-fixture corpus through the
enrichment stage and diffs every derived field against the accepted baseline.
The overwhelming majority of fixtures reproduce their baseline labels exactly.
A thin residue of rows, though, now derive a category or a counterparty name
that disagrees with the accepted answer. Each regressed row is stable - the same
fixture yields the identical wrong field every time it is replayed - and each one
hinges on a narrow, individually rare pattern in the underlying reference text
rather than on the size of the amount or on which customer it belongs to.
Ordinary purchases, routine transfers and everyday deposits all reproduce
baseline, which is why the aggregate diff read clean until these edge fixtures
were isolated.

The findings are recorded in the order they surfaced. QA has not traced any of
them to a root cause; that is left to engineering. Acceptance for this build is
simply that every listed finding derives its baseline field again and that no
fixture already matching baseline moves.

## Findings

**F-1.** A cheque-type debit whose statement note carries nothing but the
instrument's own number - a short, bare run of digits with no other text sitting
beside it - is landing in the generic transfer bucket. Cheque debits whose notes
are shaped even slightly differently keep their correct cheque label, so the miss
is confined to this one bare-number note form.

**F-2.** On a cleared cheque, the counterparty column is coming back with an
internal clearing tag in place of the account-holder's name. The affected rows
all share one raw-narration layout, copied here from a fixture:

> `CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-RAVI KUMAR`

For this layout the field is returning a fragment of the reference instead of the
name that should be lifted from it.

**F-3.** A slice of inbound electronic-transfer credits - the plain
national-transfer kind - are arriving with the counterparty-name column left
completely blank. The category on these rows is right; it is only the name that
goes missing. Other electronic-transfer credits, whose references are laid out
differently, still resolve their names normally, so this is not a blanket failure
of name extraction.

**F-4.** An incoming person-to-person instant-payment credit is showing a bare
reference number where the sender's name belongs. The value that surfaces is a
fragment of the very reference string the name should have been read from;
neighbouring instant-payment layouts still resolve their names correctly.

**F-5.** A small nominal deposit that a bank posts purely to confirm an account
is reachable - the token "is this account live" credit rather than a real
payment - is being filed as an ordinary transfer instead of being recognised as
an account-verification entry. Ordinary deposits are untouched; only these token
confirmation credits regressed.

## Exit criteria

The enrichment path is fully deterministic and runs offline, so each finding
above is reproducible on demand from the fixture that triggered it. Restore the
correct category and counterparty on the listed forms without disturbing any
fixture that already agrees with baseline. A change that rescues these rows but
shifts the label or the name of ordinary, currently-correct traffic does not meet
acceptance: the bar is that the specific regressions listed here clear and
everything else stays exactly where the baseline has it.
I'll explore the codebase to locate the transaction-categorization enrichment logic and the fixtures behind these RC 2.14 findings.

# Transaction Categorization / Enrichment — Codebase Report

## 1. Overall project structure

Flask microservice that enriches bank transactions (category, subcategory, counterparty/`partyName`, merchant type, optional PFM labels).

```
/app
├── Dockerfile                          # python:3.9.2, gunicorn :9898
├── .gitignore
└── categorizationapp/
    ├── setup.py                        # Flask, pandas, fuzzywuzzy, sklearn…
    └── categorizationapp/
        ├── __init__.py                 # Flask app
        ├── Controller.py               # /categorizeTransaction, /recurrentTransactions
        ├── BankScripts/                # 35 bank-specific parsers
        └── UtilityScripts/             # shared enrichment
```

| Path | Role |
|------|------|
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/Controller.py` | HTTP routing; bank dispatch; pipeline orchestration |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/*.py` | Per-bank `transactionCategory` + initial `partyName` |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/Purpose.py` | Cross-bank subcategory / merchant purpose |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/CleanName.py` | Merchant/counterparty name normalization (~2k lines) |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/BankRegexConstants.py` | Bank-specific regexes (CHQ, NEFT, ACC_VERIF, …) |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/RegexConstants.py` | Merchant/purpose keyword regexes |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/AppUtil.py` | `sep_by_dash`, `sep_by_`, `py_extract`, `clean_input_df` |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/SalaryDetection.py` | Heuristic salary |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/InternalPayment.py` | Self-transfer via account-holder fuzzy match |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/PFMCategorization.py` | PFM rollup (optional) |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/SimpleDescription.py` | Human-readable description |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/TransactionCategoryEnums.py` | Display labels for categories |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/TransactionSubcategoryEnums.py` | Subcategory labels |

**Git history:** single commit `047782b import codebase` — no diff history to attribute F-1…F-5 to a recent change. All “regressions” look like long-standing logic gaps in this snapshot.

---

## 2. How categorization works

### Pipeline (`Controller.categorizeTransaction`)

For each bank (same pattern for all ~35):

1. `AppUtil.clean_input_df` — strip description, numeric amount/balance  
2. **Bank script** — set `transactionCategory` (default **`TRANSFER`**), optional bank `transactionSubcategory`, extract `partyName`  
3. If `CREDIT_CARD`: `card_clean_names` → `card_purpose`  
4. **`purpose()`** — enrich subcategory/merchant; can override category (e.g. loan ₹1 → account verification)  
5. **`clean_names()`** — normalize known merchants into clean `partyName`  
6. Optional `internal_payment` (needs `accountHolder`)  
7. Optional `salary_detection` (`SAVING` only)  
8. Optional `pfm_categorization` + `simple_description` if `isPFMEnabled`

### Category assignment pattern

Every bank script builds ordered `conditions_choices` lists and applies:

```python
transactions['transactionCategory'] = np.select(conditions, choices, default="TRANSFER")
```

**First matching condition wins.** Unmatched → generic `TRANSFER`.

### Counterparty (`partyName`) derivation

Bank scripts parse `description` (sometimes `remark`) with split helpers:

| Helper | Split on |
|--------|----------|
| `sep_by_dash(desc, n1, n2)` | `-` |
| `sep_by_(desc, n1, n2)` | `/` |
| `sep_by_colon` / `_` / `~` / `*` | respective delimiter |
| `py_extract(desc, pat, index)` | regex capture |

Then title-case / strip junk; `CleanName.clean_names` maps merchants (Netflix, BESCOM, etc.).

### Subcategory / purpose

`Purpose.purpose()` matches description/`partyName` against huge keyword regexes in `RegexConstants.py` (salary, loan, fuel, rent, …). Also:

- LOAN + amount ∈ {1, -1} → category `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION`  
- Categories matching `VERIFICATION|CHARGES|BOUNCE|…` clear subcategory  

---

## 3. Test fixtures / baseline / regression tests

**None in this repo.**

- No `test/`, `tests/`, `*fixture*`, baseline CSVs/JSON, or pytest/unittest setup  
- No README with test commands  
- No sample payloads  

### How you can exercise the service

```bash
# install & run
cd /app/categorizationapp && pip3 install -e .
# or via Docker
docker build -t categorizationapp /app
docker run -p 9898:9898 categorizationapp

# health
curl http://localhost:9898/

# categorize (shape)
curl -X POST http://localhost:9898/categorizeTransaction \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "bank": "HDFC",
    "acc_type": "SAVING",
    "accountUID": "u1",
    "accountHolder": "",
    "isPFMEnabled": false,
    "transactions": [{
      "description": "CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-RAVI KUMAR",
      "amount": 5000,
      "type": "DEBIT",
      "remark": "",
      "balanceAfterTransaction": 1000,
      "transactionDate": "2024-01-01"
    }]
  }'
```

There is **no** in-repo test command for F-1…F-5. You would need an external baseline suite or ad-hoc curls/scripts against bank scripts.

---

## 4. Findings F-1 through F-5 (root causes)

### F-1: Cheque debit with bare number note → generic `TRANSFER`

**Intent:** Many banks encode cheque number only in `remark` (e.g. `123456`) with a non-cheque description.

**Banks that treat bare numeric remark as cheque:**

| Bank | Pattern |
|------|---------|
| YES, UCO | `remark ^[0-9]{3,6}$` → CHEQUE_PAID/DEPOSIT |
| Axis, BOM, Indusind | `^[0-9]{5,6}$` |
| Kotak, BOB | `^[0-9]{3,5}$` |
| PNB | debit `^[0-9]{5}$`, credit `^[0-9]{5,6}$` |
| RBL | only `^[0-9]{1,3}$` (too short for typical 6-digit cheques) |
| TMB | `^[0-9]{5,}/` |

**Banks that do *not* map bare-number remarks to cheque (default `TRANSFER`):**  
HDFC, ICICI, SBI, Canara, Federal, IDBI, IDFC, Union (remark used only for partyName on TRANSFER), Andhra, BOI, Citi, CityUnion, DCB, Karnataka, Saraswat, SCB, Syndicate, Bandhan, AuSFB, Central, Indian, SVC, Paytm, …

**HDFC specifically:** only cheque-from-remark for **16-digit zero-padded credit** remarks (`^[0]{11}[0-9]{5}`) as `CHEQUE_DEPOSIT` — **no debit bare-number rule**.

**Obvious bug / gap:** Incomplete coverage of “remark = cheque number only” across major banks; digit-length windows differ (3–6 vs 5–6 vs 1–3), so same remark misclassifies depending on bank.

---

### F-2: `CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-RAVI KUMAR` → internal clearing tag, not “Ravi Kumar”

**Primary locus:** `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/HDFC.py` + `BankRegexConstants.py` HDFC cheque patterns.

Verified split behavior:

```
"CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-RAVI KUMAR".split('-')
→ ['CHQ PAID', 'MICR CLG', 'RAVI KUMAR']
```

| Step | What happens |
|------|----------------|
| Category | Matches `CHQ` / `Chq Paid` → `CHEQUE_PAID` (OK) |
| `HDFC_CHQ_PATTERN6` | Only `CHQ PAID-MICR CTS` — **not** `MICR CLG` → no match |
| Line 163 | Any `CHQ PAID-` → `sep_by_dash(desc, 3, 4)` → **empty** (name is index **2**) |
| Line 193 | PATTERN6 path uses index 3,4 — wrong for 3-segment layout even for CTS |
| Line 260 cleanup | `partyName contains "Micr Clg\|Chq Paid"` → **force blank** |

If extraction ever leaves `MICR CLG` as partyName (e.g. wrong dash index), cleanup **wipes it** rather than stripping the clearing prefix and keeping the payee.

**Correct extraction for this layout:** `sep_by_dash(..., 2, 3)` → `RAVI KUMAR`, or a dedicated regex  
`CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-(.+)` / `CHQ PAID-MICR\s+CLG-(.+)`.

**Also missing pattern:** `HDFC_CHQ_PATTERN6` should cover `MICR CLG` alongside `MICR CTS`.

---

### F-3: Inbound electronic-transfer credits — blank counterparty

Several interacting issues:

**ICICI** (`ICICI.py`):

- Inbound NEFT often `INF/NEFT/...`; a better extract (`sep_by_` index 4) is **commented out**:
  ```python
  # [ ... "^INF/NEFT/" ... sep_by_(...,4,5)], #comment out for this
  ```
- Active rule uses index 3, which frequently hits UTR/IFSC/ref, not name.
- Aggressive cleanup blanks any `partyName` with **6+ digits**:
  ```python
  partyName.str.contains("[0-9]{6,}|...") → ""
  ```
  So a half-correct extract that still contains a ref becomes **empty**.

**SBI NEFT:** default `sep_by_star(..., 3, 4)` + strip digits/punctuation — inbound layouts without `*` segments yield empty.

**HDFC NEFT:** assumes dash layout `NEFT CR-...-NAME-...`; non-conforming credits miss extractors.

**YES IMPS:** category detects IMPS, but party-name block has `#imps` with **no rules** under it — IMPS party stays blank.

**Cross-cutting:** `np.select` default for partyName is `""`; missed layout → blank, not fallback to description.

---

### F-4: P2P UPI credit shows bare reference instead of sender name

UPI extraction is almost always a fixed slash/dash index:

| Bank | UPI party rule | Failure mode |
|------|----------------|--------------|
| ICICI / SBI / Axis | `sep_by_(desc, 3, 4)` | Layout without CR/DR at [2] puts **name at [2], bank/ref at [3]** → bank code or ref |
| HDFC | `sep_by_dash(desc, 1, 2)` for `^UPI-` | Usually name, but some layouts put ref in segment 1 |
| YES | Only `UPI/[0-9]+/From:` / `FROM:` | Other YES UPI formats → blank or wrong |

Example (ICICI/SBI-style):

```
UPI/412345678901/RAVI KUMAR/SBIN.../Payment
  index 3 → SBIN...   (wrong)
  index 2 → RAVI KUMAR (correct)
UPI/412345678901/CR/RAVI KUMAR/SBIN...
  index 3 → RAVI KUMAR (correct)
```

**ICICI** later blanks pure long-digit partyNames (`[0-9]{6,}`), so F-4 may appear as **blank** rather than bare ref on ICICI; on banks without that scrub (or when ref is alphanumeric), **bare RRN/UTR stays as `partyName`**.

HDFC has a partial fix (if UPI party looks numeric, retry dash segment 2) but only for digit-heavy names, not all P2P layouts.

---

### F-5: Account-verification token deposit filed as ordinary transfer

Penny-drop / ₹1 credits should become `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION`.

**Broken amount checks (numeric vs string):**  
`clean_input_df` coerces `amount` to **numeric**, but:

```python
# BankOfMaharashtra.py, Indusind.py
transactions.amount.isin(["1","-1"])   # always False for float 1.0
```

So keyword-based verification never fires on those banks for real ₹1 txns.

**Canara off-by-one:**

```python
# Canara.py
BANK_VERIF & amount.lt(1)   # ₹1 does NOT match; only amount < 1
```

Should be `.lt(2)` (like HDFC/RBL/PNB) or `.isin([1,-1])` / `.eq(1)`.

**Over-narrow keyword regexes:**

- YES: only `"Acc validation"`  
- SBI: `ACC_VERIF` but **credit + amount.eq(1)** only  
- Kotak: only two hard-coded patterns (`Karz Xx4002`, `^Received from [A-Z]` + ₹1)  
- Generic `BANK_VER` is broad (`verif|valid|pennydrop|…`) but only used where wired correctly  

**Purpose.py secondary path** only remaps if subcategory already `LOAN` and amount 1/-1 — does not catch ordinary IMPS/NEFT/UPI ₹1 transfers labeled `TRANSFER`/`IMPS`/`NEFT`.

**Paytm** is one of the few that maps bare `IMPS` + amount 1 credit → `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION`.

---

## 5. Key regexes / patterns (quick reference)

```text
# Account verification (BankRegexConstants.py)
ACC_VERIF      = Account va|Bank det|AccVerify|pennyd|...|/bav|BANK DETAILS VALID
BANK_VER       = PennyD|AccVeri|verif|pennydrop|valida|GOOGLE TEM|BENE NAME|...
BANK_VER_ICICI = Account Va|/BAV-|/BV[0-9]|TestVPA|PennyD|...
BANK_VERIF     = verif|nydrop|valida|...|IMPS Txn   # Canara (with broken lt(1))
ACC_VERI_YES   = Acc validation

# HDFC cheque party (broken for MICR CLG)
HDFC_CHQ_PATTERN6 = Chq Paid-MICR CTS|CHQ PAID-MICR CTS   # missing MICR CLG
HDFC cleanup      = Micr Clg|Chq Paid → blank partyName

# Bare cheque number remarks (examples)
YES/UCO:  ^[0-9]{3,6}$
Axis:     ^[0-9]{5,6}$
Kotak:    ^[0-9]{3,5}$
RBL:      ^[0-9]{1,3}$   # likely too short

# Default category
np.select(..., default="TRANSFER")
```

---

## 6. Recent changes / regression history

**Not available.** Git has only the initial import. F-1…F-5 cannot be blamed on a later commit inside this tree; they read as **latent defects** in the imported logic (wrong dash indices, string/numeric amount mismatch, incomplete bank coverage, commented-out extractors).

---

## 7. Summary of obvious bugs tied to F-1…F-5

| ID | Severity | Location | Bug |
|----|----------|----------|-----|
| F-1 | High | Many `BankScripts` (esp. HDFC/ICICI/SBI/Canara) | No (or incomplete) bare numeric `remark` → `CHEQUE_*`; default `TRANSFER` |
| F-2 | High | `HDFC.py` L163, L193, L260; `HDFC_CHQ_PATTERN6` | Wrong dash index for `CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-NAME`; CTS-only pattern; cleanup blanks `Micr Clg` instead of stripping prefix |
| F-3 | High | `ICICI.py` (commented INF/NEFT rule + digit wipe); `YES.py` empty IMPS party block; SBI/HDFC NEFT layout assumptions | Inbound NEFT/IMPS party often empty |
| F-4 | High | ICICI/SBI/Axis UPI `sep_by_(…,3,4)` | Assumes CR/DR segment; P2P without it yields ref/IFSC as name |
| F-5 | High | `Canara.py` `amount.lt(1)`; BOM/Indusind `isin(["1","-1"])` | ₹1 verification never matches after numeric cast; narrow bank keywords |

### Highest-confidence fixes (if implementing)

1. **F-2:** Add `CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-(.*)` (and/or use dash index 2); stop blanking entire party when it contains `Micr Clg` — strip clearing tokens only.  
2. **F-5:** Use numeric `amount.isin([1, -1])` or `abs(amount)==1` everywhere; Canara → `lt(2)` or `eq(1)`.  
3. **F-1:** Add shared bare-remark cheque rule (e.g. `remark ~ ^\d{4,6}$` + debit/credit) for banks that use cheque-number remarks.  
4. **F-3/F-4:** Layout-aware UPI/NEFT extractors (detect CR/DR vs name position); don’t default blank when a later alphabetic segment exists; restore ICICI `INF/NEFT` name index carefully so refs aren’t kept as names.

---

## 8. Test commands

**In-repo:** none.

**Runtime smoke:**

```bash
pip3 install -e /app/categorizationapp
cd /app/categorizationapp && gunicorn -w 1 -b 0.0.0.0:9898 categorizationapp:app
# POST /categorizeTransaction as above
```

**Direct unit-style (no server):** import `categorize_HDFC_transactions` / etc. with a one-row DataFrame — still no packaged fixtures.

---

**Bottom line:** This is a regex/`np.select` enrichment service with bank-specific narration parsers. Categories and counterparties are derived almost entirely from description/remark patterns. There are **no tests or baselines** in-tree. F-1…F-5 map cleanly to concrete gaps in cheque-remark handling, HDFC MICR CLG party extraction, NEFT/UPI segment indexing, and broken ₹1 account-verification amount checks.
